_schema_note: Template scenarios for the WhatsApp Template Create E2E suite (tests/whatsapp/templates/test_whatsapp_template_create_flow.py::test_e2e_template_submit). The 'components' list intentionally mirrors Meta's real WhatsApp Business Template API JSON shape (category/language/components[BODY|FOOTER|BUTTONS|CAROUSEL]) -- that shape was provided directly by the project owner as a genuine template payload example, not invented here. Fields that have no equivalent in Meta's schema but are specific to this app's own Create-page UI (catalog_type, content_id, mpm_section_title, lto_expiry_days, product_carousel_button_type, etc.) live under the separate 'gts_fields' object on each entry so the two are never confused. Every entry's 'confirmed' flag and 'notes' field record exactly what real evidence backs it -- per this project's standing rule, nothing here is a guess presented as fact. 'sub_category_selection' ('optional', the default, or 'required') preserves a real distinction from the original hand-written tests: for Custom Message/Order Details/Order Status, selecting the sub_category was always best-effort (select it if the select happens to be present, but never skip the test if it isn't); for every other sub_category the select is load-bearing to reach the fields under test, so the test skips outright if it isn't present. 'sub_category_force_select' (default false) is a separate, narrower flag confirmed necessary only for conversation_cta_url_button by directly watching a --headed run: unlike UTILITY/Custom Message (where clicking an already-selected option DESELECTS it -- a real bug worked around in ensure_sub_category_selected), CONVERSATION/CTA URL Button's single-option dropdown shows the right text by default but apparently never actually commits it to the Livewire model until a real click fires -- the opposite symptom. Setting this true forces the click even when the display text already matches.
